The three consecutive even integers can be written as $2k, 2k+2, 2k+4$, so their product is

$$2k(2k+2)(2k+4) = 8\,k(k+1)(k+2).$$

Let $P = k(k+1)(k+2)$, so the product is $8P$.

**Range:** A 6-digit number starting with 2 lies in $[200000, 299999]$, so $25000 \le P \le 37499$.

**Last digit:** $8P$ must end in 2, so $8P \equiv 2 \pmod{10}$. Dividing by 2 gives $4P \equiv 1 \pmod 5$, so $P \equiv 4 \pmod 5$.

**Check candidates:** Since $k^3 \approx P$, the relevant values are about $k = 28$ to $33$.

| $k$ | $P = k(k+1)(k+2)$ | $P \bmod 5$ | $8P$ | In range? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 28 | 24360 | 0 | 194880 | No (below 200000) |
| 29 | 26970 | 0 | 215760 | Fails ends-in-2 test |
| 30 | 29760 | 0 | 238080 | Fails ends-in-2 test |
| 31 | 32736 | 1 | 261888 | Fails ends-in-2 test |
| 32 | 35904 | 4 | 287232 | Yes |
| 33 | 39270 | — | 314160 | No (above 299999) |

Only $k = 32$ works. The even integers are $64, 66, 68$, and

$$64 \cdot 66 \cdot 68 = 287232.$$

The number starts with 2 and ends with 2, and no other 6-digit value in range qualifies.

ANSWER: 287232
